chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Isma'il ibn Mihran, from Abu Sa'id al-Qammad, from Aban ibn Taghlib, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

When the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) was taken on the Night Journey, he said: 'O Lord, what is the state of the believer in Your presence?' He said: 'O Muhammad, whoever dishonors a friend of Mine, he has declared war against Me, and I am the quickest to aiding My friends. And I do not hesitate in doing anything as I hesitate regarding the death of the believer, who dislikes death, and I dislike disappointing him.'

And among My believing servants is one for whom wealth is not made correct except by richness, and if I were to turn him to other than that, he would be destroyed. And among My believing servants is one for whom poverty is not made correct except by poverty, and if I were to turn him to other than that, he would be destroyed.

And a servant does not draw near to Me with anything more beloved to Me than what I have obligated upon him. And indeed, he draws near to Me with the voluntary [acts] until I love him. So when I love him, I become his hearing with which he hears, and his sight with which he sees, and his tongue with which he speaks, and his hand with which he grasps. If he calls upon Me, I answer him, and if he asks Me, I give him.
ai.seo_question: What is the status of the believer in the presence of God according to the Mi'raj narrative?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated by Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) from the Prophet’s Mi'raj, elucidates the concept of *al-Walayah* by stating that insulting a believer is akin to declaring war on God, while voluntary acts (*nawafil*) elevate the servant to the station of *Fanā’* (annihilation in God). It further clarifies divine wisdom in varying states of wealth and poverty for different believers, culminating in the promise that God becomes the servant’s senses and limbs, directly answering their calls. This narrative is foundational in Shia theology for understanding the spiritual hierarchy and the intimate connection between the Divine and the faithful.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Ismail Bin Mihran, from Abu Saeed Al Qammat, from Aban Bin Taghlub, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’farasws having said: ‘When there was Ascension (Mi’raj) with the Prophetsaww, hesaww said: ‘O Lordazwj!

What is the state of the Momin in Yourazwj Presence?’ Heazwj Said: “O Muhammadsaww! The one who despises a friend of Mineazwj, so he has declared a war against Meazwj and Iazwj am the Quickest to Helping Myazwj friends and Iazwj do not Hesitate from anything which Iazwj Do like Iazwj Hesitate from the death of the Momin. He dislikes the death and Iazwj Dislike Disappointing him.

And from Myazwj Momineen servants there is one for whom it is not correct except for the riches, and were Iazwj to Exchange it to other than that, he would be destroyed; and from Myazwj Momineen servants there is one for whom it is not correct except for the poverty, and were Iazwj to Exchange it to other than that, he would be destroyed.

And a servant will not (be able to) come near to Meazwj with anything more Beloved to Meazwj than what Iazwj have Obligated upon him, and let him come closer to Meazwj with the Optional (Salāt) until Iazwj Love him. So when Iazwj do Love him, Iazwj would be the hearing which he listens with, and his vision which he sees with, and his tongue which he speaks with, and his hand which he strikes with. If he were to supplicate to Meazwj, Iazwj would Answer him, and if he were to ask Meazwj, Iazwj would Give it to him”’.
en.sarwar: 8. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from Isma’il ibn Mehran from abu Sa’id al-Qammat from Aban ibn Taghlib from abu Ja’far (a.s.) who has said the following:

“When the Holy Prophet was taken to visit the heavens, he asked, ‘O Lord, how is the condition of the believers before you?’ He (Allah) said, ‘O Muhammad, whoever insults any of My friends has declared war against Me. I am the quickest to help My friends. I have not hesitated in any of My acts as much as I do at the time of the death of a believer who dislikes death and I dislike to disappoint him.

Of My believing servants there are those who do not perform well without wealth and if I change his condition he is destroyed. Also among My believing servants are those who do not perform well unless they are poor and, if I change their condition to something else, they are destroyed.

For seeking nearness to Me there is no better means for My servant than to fulfill what 1 have made obligatory for them and that he should seek nearness to Me through performing optional acts of worship so I will love him. When I will love him I will be his ears with which he will hear, his eyes with which he will see, his tongue with which he will speak and his hands with which he will perform his activities. Whenever he prays I will answer him and, whenever he asks a favor, I will grant him.’”
